title: Set-valued ind-finite etale monodromy equivalence
statement: Let $X$ be a connected Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $\Pi=\pi_1(X,x)$, with the profinite topology of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $\mathcal L(X)$ be the full category of set sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] that are small filtered colimits of sheaves represented by finite etale $X$-schemes [def-per-ind-finite-etale-local-system, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Let $\mathcal A(\Pi)$ have as objects arbitrary sets with a $\Pi$-action whose point stabilizers are open, and as arrows equivariant maps; the underlying sets are given the discrete topology. The geometric-stalk functor $F\mapsto F_x$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] has a natural $\Pi$-action and is an equivalence $\mathcal L(X)\simeq\mathcal A(\Pi)$. On finite etale representables it agrees with the finite fibre functor of [def-galois-fibre-functor]. For every small filtered diagram of finite etale $X$-schemes $(P_i)$, with colimit $F=\varinjlim_i h_{P_i}$ in ambient set sheaves, the canonical map $\varinjlim_i |(P_i)_x|\to F_x$ is a $\Pi$-equivariant bijection, where the colimit on the left is the ordinary set colimit with its induced action.

source.place: Expose XVII, Propositions 7.2.2 and 7.2.3, p. 301; passage of the finite fibre equivalence to ind-objects, including the filtered-presentation fibre comparison.
